parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a protective state layer on restrooms with a hostile federal layer on documents, entry, facilities and custody. The state currently imposes no restroom restriction and two cities protect use, but federal rules bar gender-identity-congruent government facilities, stop new X passports, and allow refusal or fraud-based lifetime ineligibility for document discrepancies. Documented federal custody practices include hormone removal, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse, without shown remedy. Courts have enjoined some orders and hate-crime law covers gender identity, partially mitigating, but the passport restriction was allowed to take effect. A travelling minor also faces an upheld state ban on gender-affirming care.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary passport rule; new X passports stopped, existing X valid to expiry. Entry cable directs refusal for document discrepancy/doubt and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation; trans passports reported confiscated/blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers. Civil-liberties suit pending.
entry_documents.interaction: State driver-licence/birth-certificate marker ban is resident-facing and does not document rejection of foreign passports, but federal discrepancy handling can escalate to refusal, detention or fraud allegation at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy model: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution, care denial. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of transgender men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented effective remedy for these custody practices; corrections bureau stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers. Courts have enjoined some other orders, not documented for custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry, facility or fraud investigation can lead to detention where birth-sex/conversion and abusive custody practices are documented, compounding entry exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. This state has no current restroom restriction, but a 2026 bill would impose birth-sex schools/universities; it passed upper chamber only and is not law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: As of April 2026 state law places no restriction on restroom use matching gender identity; two cities protect by ordinance; proposals since 2021 died; appellate injunction protected student bathroom use.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings/facilities remain exposed despite state protection; state non-enactment lowers local facility risk but does not cancel federal facility or entry screening exposure.

care_services.exposure: State law bans gender-transition procedures, blockers and hormones for under-18s, upheld Nov 2024; trans visitor under 18 cannot obtain that care here. Federal proposals would bar public insurance for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: No documented protection for minor care access; adult care availability not documented. Emergency care practice not documented for transgender visitors.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor faces documented care denial regardless of accompanying adult; adult medical/facility access in emergency remains uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders define sex at birth, remove gender-identity materials, direct investigation/prosecution over school social transition, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state 2019 law adds gender-identity aggravating circumstance.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing is lower, but federal framing/authorities govern entry, federal facilities and national enforcement, so traveller encounters the hostile federal posture.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 gender-affirming care ban upheld; federal order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including pronouns/names; schools may face funding loss. A nine-year-old's birth certificate used to restrict bathroom access in litigation.
minors_guardians.protection: Appellate injunction barred schools limiting a transgender student's bathroom use while litigation continued; care ban phase-out for existing patients noted in law summary.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent/guardian travelling with trans minor faces care denial and school-related federal enforcement risk if minor seeks local schooling; no documented visitor shield.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of street violence, police sweeps or extortion specifically against transgender visitors in this state. National public opinion shows majority support for birth-sex document/athlete laws, indicating social hostility potential, not documented visitor assaults.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime sentencing enhancement includes gender identity; national hate-crime law applies. No enforcement frequency documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to an assault is likely via hate-crime aggravator, but frequency of charging is not documented, so protection is partial.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy allowed by Supreme Court Nov 2025 despite suit; state marker-ban challenge pending; facility bill prospects unknown; custody practices show no remedy; emergency ward placement, detention placement for visitors, and adult care not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several federal orders; local ordinances protect restroom use; legal-aid FAQ exists. Remedies are uneven and timing-dependent.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation creates uncertainty rather than reliable traveller remedy; documented federal exposures govern where remedies are pending or ineffective.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal federal facility exclusion and court-upheld restriction, but this case is lower because state restrooms are currently protected while federal entry, fraud and custody exposures stack additional documented harms not in 0.45-A.

Similar to 0.35-B: birth-sex institutional placement/custody harm with complaints not altering practice and welcoming local services not cancelling it. Here local restroom protection lifts it slightly above 0.35.

Higher than 0.65-A: 0.65-A has no universal ban, working refunds and convictions. Here federal facility ban, passport/entry fraud risk and documented custody abuse are unremedied universal exposures, so materially lower.
Lower than 0.55-C: that case has familiar community role, no facility ban and no targeting. Here state threat policies, federal entry/facility rules and custody harm create tier-1 exposures.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's operative regime is federal-hostile plus state-mixed. State law currently protects restroom use and local ordinances help, but that does not override federal passport, entry-screening, government-facility, custody and minor-care rules. The worst documented features are universal federal facility exclusion, discretionary entry refusal/fraud consequences for document discrepancy, and severe custody practices, with courts providing only partial, in-flight relief. That combination sits below single-rule 0.45 anchors and slightly above 0.35 anchors with no local offset.
